definition: DBRX is a large language model (LLM) developed by Mosaic under its parent company Databricks, released on March 27, 2024 under the Databricks Open Model License.
details: It is a mixture-of-experts transformer model, with 132 billion parameters in total. 36 billion parameters (4 out of 16 experts) are active for each token. The released model comes in either a base foundation model version or an instruction-tuned variant. At the time of its release, DBRX outperformed prominent models such as Meta's Llama 2, Mistral AI's Mixtral, and xAI's Grok-1, in several benchmarks ranging from language understanding, programming ability and mathematics. It was trained for 2.5 months and reported using on 3,072 Nvidia H100s connected by 3.2 terabytes per second bandwidth (InfiniBand), for a training cost of US$10M.
story: Think of a grammar teacher who never memorized a rule but can still tell you when a sentence sounds wrong. The machine learns language the way you did — by hearing so much of it that the patterns sink in. It figures out meaning by noticing which words like to travel together. The machine learns to read between the lines by reading an impossible number of lines. And that is DBRX — teaching a machine to read between the lines.
